purpose: A part-to-whole chart drawn as a ring (donut) or a disc (pie): one slice per series, the total in the center, a legend beside it. It shares the cartesian chart's data model, palette, legend behavior and loading / empty / error surface, so a dashboard reads as one system. Each slice is the sum of its series values, so a time series passes straight in as its share of the range.
useWhen: Share of a small whole at a glance: top countries by blocked threats, traffic by protocol, cache hit versus miss.
A dashboard card where the total is the headline and the split is the context.
avoidWhen: Comparing close values or more than six slices → use `chart` with horizontal bars; angles are hard to compare.
Two slices → use `stat-tile` with the ratio; a two-slice pie says less than the number.
related: chart` — the cartesian sibling; same series model, so a dataset moves between them without reshaping.
chart-card` — the box a dashboard donut sits in.
stat-tile` — the total alone, with a delta.
bestPractices: Keep it to six slices or fewer; the seventh and beyond fold into Other automatically.
Order series by size so the largest slice starts at the top.
Use the center for the total and let hover or focus swap it to the active slice.
Pair it with the bar form of the same data when exact ranks matter (the console's country pie plus ordered bar).
